articles.title: Diamond Lattice
articles.summary: Crisp rhombus grid, flat polished-steel cells, thin bright outlines, one accent cell in seven. Gone; reads as a plain surface with, at best, a faint cross-hatched sheen in the hot spot.
articles.what: R6 owner rebuild — CLEAN sharp rhombus lattice grid with crisp 1px polyline outlines, uniform per-cell fill from a tight polished-steel palette + every 7th cell as a brig Up close: Hairline crossing lines forming a very fine diamond or quilt grid, with cells around 18-25 px; the lines are 1 px and only just visible in the highlight band. Cell fills are not distinguishable, so no accent cells show. From a distance: Gone; reads as a plain surface with, at best, a faint cross-hatched sheen in the hot spot. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Precision & Guilloché (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: body, roof, hero panel.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Precision & Guilloché", or search for "Diamond Lattice".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood and roof on metallic or chrome bases where the thin lines show
Hero panels in clean luxury builds
Practically invisible, a faint grid trace
Pairs well with: gloss, metallic, chrome.
pitfalls: Not diamond plate: no raised diamonds, only hairline lines
Not a harlequin paint pattern: adds no colour fill
Avoid: too regular for organic shapes, accent cells can clash.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.title: Add it as an overlay

examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.
